bands.1:
Five badges! Mo makes a banana-and-tuna pie. Nobody eats it.

Kaydence Kray is on deck. She films everything.

A gold pedal boat comes out of the dark. A silver robot is pedalling it. His left hand is a feather duster.

"Good evening," says the robot. "I am BOLT-9, Maxx's butler. I rate your boat three out of ten."

"Hello, Bolt," says Wren. "He was my nanny-bot. He read me stories, then rated them."

"Your brother wants you home, Miss Wren," says BOLT-9.

"She's not going," you say. "She's crew."

A screen on his chest lights up. It is Maxx.

"Fine," snaps Maxx. "Then delete her. Wipe every memory of Wrennie. Now!"

BOLT-9's eyes flicker. A picture shines on the sail. Little Wren and little Max feed a baby possum in a shoebox.

"When I grow up," says little Max, "I will save every animal in the world."

Wren's eyes fill with tears.

"Very good, sir," says BOLT-9. Then he stops.

"The Reef Rays lost by a hundred," whispers Tully.

"TULLY!"

"No," says BOLT-9.

"What do you mean, NO?" yells Maxx.

"It is the opposite of yes, sir. Zero out of ten." He switches Maxx off with his duster.

"Captain, may I join your crew?" asks BOLT-9. "I have recorded everything Maxx has ever done."

"Everything?" asks Kaydence. "Where he keeps stuff? His passwords?"

BOLT-9 looks at her. "I rate your ring light nine out of ten."

"Why did the robot go on holiday?" asks Mo. "To recharge!"

"Two out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo is thrilled.

"Welcome aboard," you say. Wren hugs him.

Later, BOLT-9 finds you alone.

"Remember the photo of your boat that Maxx showed his fans?" he says. "He did not take it. Someone sent it to him."

"Who?"

"He took that call in secret."

Behind you, a little red light blinks. Kaydence's camera is filming.

"Your brother requests your return," says BOLT-9. "I have packed your toothbrush and your possum slippers."

The whole crew steps in front of Wren.

"Well? Is she coming or not?" he snaps.

"TULLY!"

"The butler just rage-quit the final boss!" says Zed.

"He took that call in private. Even I was sent out of the room."

bands.4:
Five badges! Mo has baked a banana-and-tuna pie to celebrate. It smells like a fish that has spent a long holiday at a fruit shop, and the crust has a worrying shine. Nobody eats it, but everyone says thank you, which is almost the same thing.

Kaydence Kray is on deck, filming for her channel. Her purple speedboat, the Clickbait, is tied up alongside the Soggy Biscuit, its ring lights glowing. Since she climbed aboard and offered to help, she has been extremely helpful, which mostly means filming.

"Statistically," says Tully, "she has filmed 97 per cent of everything we've done. The other 3 per cent was Mo's cooking, which she refused to point a camera at."

Then a gold pedal boat squeaks out of the darkness. A tall silver robot is pedalling it, sitting perfectly upright in a neat bow tie. His left hand is a feather duster.

"Good evening," says the robot, with a small bow. "I am BOLT-9, butler to Mr Maxx Vantablack. I rate your boat three out of ten. The leak is charming."

His glowing eyes land on Wren. "Miss Wren. You have grown four centimetres."

"Hello, Bolt," says Wren softly. She turns to the crew. "He was my nanny-bot when I was little. He read me bedtime stories, then rated them."

"Your brother requests your return," says BOLT-9. "I have packed your toothbrush and your possum slippers."

The whole crew steps in front of Wren, shoulder to shoulder, even Mo, who is still holding the pie.

"She's not going anywhere," you say. "She's crew."

"Understood, Captain. I rate that answer ten out of ten."

The screen on his chest crackles into life. It's Maxx, wrapped in a gold dressing gown, wearing a gold face mask and a very sour expression.

"Well? Is she coming or not?" he snaps.

"Not, sir."

"Ugh. Plan B, then," says Maxx, inspecting his nails. "Delete her. Every memory you have of Wrennie: the birthdays, the bedtime stories, all of it. If she won't be in my family, she won't be in my story. Smash that delete button like it owes you money, Bolt!"

BOLT-9's eyes flicker. A memory beams out of them and plays across the sail like a movie: little Wren and little Max in matching pyjamas, feeding a baby possum in a shoebox with an eyedropper.

"His name is Sir Nibbles," says little Max, grinning a gap-toothed grin. "When I grow up, I'm going to save every animal in the world."

Wren's eyes fill with tears. Indi quietly starts to sketch.

"Very good, sir," says BOLT-9. Then he goes completely, unbearably silent.

Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays just lost by a hundred," she whispers.

"TULLY!"

"No," says BOLT-9.

"What do you mean, NO?" shrieks Maxx.

"It is the opposite of yes, sir. I rate this order zero out of ten." BOLT-9 gives the screen a firm dusting, and Maxx vanishes mid-shriek.

"The butler just rage-quit the final boss!" says Zed, delighted.

"Robots can say no?" says Gus. "That's not science. Actually, hang on, that's brilliant science."

"Captain, I hereby resign as Mr Vantablack's butler," says BOLT-9, "and I would like to apply for a position on your crew. I can dust, iron and remember. I have recorded everything Mr Vantablack has ever done. Every net. Every onion. Every fake tear. Forty thousand hours, filed by how shiny his hair was that day."

"Everything?" Kaydence pushes her camera right up to his face. "Like where he keeps stuff? His passwords?"

BOLT-9 turns his head very slowly towards her. "I rate your ring light nine out of ten, Miss Kray." He doesn't rate anything else about her.

"Why did the robot go on holiday?" asks Mo. "It needed to recharge!"

"Two out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo looks thrilled. Nobody has ever given him a two before.

"Welcome aboard, BOLT-9," you say. Wren throws her arms round him, and he dusts the top of her head very gently, the way he must have done when she was small.

Later that night, BOLT-9 finds you alone at the wheel.

"One more thing, Captain," he says quietly. "The photo of this boat that Mr Vantablack showed his viewers, on the day you first set sail. He did not take it. Someone sent it to him."

"Who?"

"He took that call in private. Even I was sent out of the room."

Behind you, on the dark deck, a small red light is blinking. Kaydence's camera is filming.
